title: Dal Makhani at Home
subtitle: Black lentils and kidney beans slow-cooked in a rich, buttery tomato sauce
excerpt: Whole black lentils and kidney beans simmered for hours in a spiced tomato base, then finished with butter and cream. The slow cook is what makes it. This is a weekend dal.
sourceNotes: Punjabi restaurant classic adapted for the home hob. Traditionally simmered overnight; this version takes 2 hours for a close result.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost overnight and reheat slowly on the hob, adding a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Use a large stockpot. The dal improves significantly with longer slow cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make a day ahead. The flavour deepens overnight in the fridge. Reheat over a low heat.

content.text: Dal makhani is all about time. Black lentils need soaking overnight and at least 2 hours of gentle simmering to soften fully. The butter and cream go in at the end. Do not skip either.
Drain the soaked black lentils. Place in a large saucepan with 800 ml of the water. Bring to the boil. Boil hard for 10 minutes, then reduce to a low simmer.
Add the drained kidney beans to the lentils. Simmer everything together, covered, for 45 minutes. Top up with water if needed to keep the lentils submerged.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in the frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle. Add the onions and cook for 12 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the ground spices and cook for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and tomato puree. Cook for 10 minutes until thick.
Add the tomato and onion base to the lentil pot. Stir well. Add the remaining 200 ml water and the salt. Simmer uncovered on a low heat for 45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.
Use the back of a ladle to roughly mash some of the lentils against the side of the pan. This thickens the dal without making it fully smooth.
Stir in the butter and cream. Add the garam masala. Simmer for a final 10 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Serve with fresh coriander.

items.symptom: The black lentils are still firm after an hour.
items.cause: They were not soaked overnight, or the water was not boiling before the lentils went in.
items.fix: Continue simmering with the lid on, checking every 20 minutes. They will eventually soften. Add water to prevent the pan drying out.

items.cause: Not enough evaporation time or the lentils were not partially mashed.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on a medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring often, until the consistency thickens.

items.symptom: The dal tastes flat despite the long cook.
items.cause: It needs more salt or the tomato base was under-reduced.
items.fix: Add salt in small amounts, stirring and tasting between each addition. A pinch of garam masala and a knob of butter also lift a flat dal.
